title: Audit trail and anchors
summary: Inspect recorded activity and check audit history against retained evidence.

sections.title: How to use this page
paragraphs: Audit trail lists events of every stream together, newest first, and each row names its stream. Security holds sign-ins, users, roles and security settings, backups, restores, updates, exports and instrument and partner connections. Clinical holds patients, orders, specimens, results, QC, reports, billing and laboratory setup such as the catalog and the laboratory profile. Access holds who opened patient records, orders, specimens, runs, results, reports or billing, and who viewed this trail or checked its chain or anchors.

Use the filters to narrow the stream, action, record, who acted, the outcome and the days recorded; they combine, the LIS applies them before it sends a page, and Clear filters removes them all at once. Open an event for its details. Self-approvals only isolates those events. Verify chain checks one chosen stream for changed or missing events.

Audit anchors shows seals copied to backup targets. Use its verification view to compare anchor evidence and its file view to inspect export history. Exporting anchors now requires backup authority in addition to viewing access.

sections.title: Good practice
paragraphs: Use filters to answer a specific review question, and retain the relevant event identifiers and verification findings through your laboratory’s process. Viewing the trail is itself recorded.

A chain check establishes consistency of the records examined. Separately held anchors provide an additional comparison point. Neither a successful local check nor an anchor copied from the same restored data establishes that all activity was appropriate.

sections.title: If you cannot continue
paragraphs: Investigate mismatches and missing anchors before drawing a conclusion. After restore, later anchors may describe the lost interval; compare times and the recovery record. Do not remove or rewrite evidence to obtain a passing result.

pages.title: Audit trail
pages.purpose: Find attributable activity across every audit stream or in one, and verify the consistency of a chosen stream.
pages.access: View audit authority is required. Viewing the trail is itself recorded as an access event.

fields.name: Stream
fields.meaning: Category of activity under review; the page description under the title says what the chosen stream holds.
fields.values: All streams (default): every event, newest first by the time it was recorded. Security: sign-ins, users, roles and security settings; backups, restores, updates and exports; instrument and partner connections. Clinical: patients, orders, specimens, results, QC, reports and billing, and laboratory setup such as the catalog and the laboratory profile. Access: who opened patient records, orders, specimens, runs, results, reports or billing, and who viewed this audit trail or checked its chain or anchors.
fields.rules: Changing stream clears Action and Record type because their choices belong to the stream; Record ID and Self-approvals only stay. With All streams, Action and Record type offer the choices of every stream.

fields.name: Find by record ID
fields.meaning: Find events concerning one internal record identifier.
fields.values: Exact record ID supplied by the relevant record/evidence, or blank for all.
fields.rules: Optional; this is not a patient-name search. Use up to 128 lowercase letters, digits, periods, colons, hyphens or underscores. Applies after a typing pause or Enter.

fields.name: Action
fields.meaning: Narrow events to one recorded operation.
fields.values: Any action or actions actually recorded in the chosen stream, or in any stream with All streams.
fields.rules: Optional; choices come from the recorded event vocabulary.

fields.name: By
fields.meaning: Narrow events by who acted.
fields.values: Anyone (default); People only: events by signed-in users; System only: events by the LIS itself, instruments and interface partners; or one user, by name, from every account.
fields.rules: Optional. A sign-in is recorded by the system, so People only leaves sign-ins out; choose System only or Anyone to see them. Kept when the stream changes.

fields.name: Outcome
fields.meaning: Narrow events by how the recorded action ended.
fields.values: Any outcome (default); Succeeded; Failed: attempted and did not complete; Denied: refused by an authorization check, such as a missing permission.
fields.rules: Optional. Kept when the stream changes.

fields.name: Record type (More filters)
fields.meaning: Narrow events by the kind of affected record.
fields.values: Any record type or the recorded types of the chosen stream, or of every stream with All streams.
fields.rules: Optional.

fields.name: Recorded from / Recorded to (More filters)
fields.meaning: Narrow events to the days they were recorded, in the laboratory's time zone (UTC before a laboratory profile exists).
fields.values: A day as YYYY-MM-DD, typed or picked from the calendar; blank for no limit. Recorded to includes the whole of its day.
fields.rules: Optional; either end may be used alone. A day that is not a real date, a Recorded to before Recorded from, or a Recorded from after Recorded to shows a message under the field and is not applied. The calendar offers no day after today. While More filters is closed, the days applied are shown under the filter row.

fields.name: Self-approvals only
fields.meaning: Isolate actions where one person performed both steps under policy.
fields.values: Unchecked (all matching events); checked (self-approvals only).
fields.rules: Optional; use for review of permitted exceptions, not as evidence that every approval required two people.

fields.name: Seq. / Stream / Outcome
fields.meaning: Sequence number within the event's stream, the stream it belongs to, and the result of the recorded action.
fields.values: Increasing sequence number within its stream, so two streams can each have an event 5; Security, Clinical or Access; Succeeded (green badge with a check mark), Denied (amber warning badge) or Failed (red badge).
fields.rules: Read-only; denied/failed events are evidence, not completed business changes.

fields.name: Occurred / Recorded
fields.meaning: When activity occurred and when its event was recorded.
fields.values: Recorded timestamps shown to seconds.
fields.rules: Read-only; the two times have distinct meanings.

fields.name: By / Principal ID
fields.meaning: Actor responsible for the event and its stable identifier.
fields.values: User, Instrument, Partner or System with displayed name/ID.
fields.rules: Read-only; use the identifier when names alone are ambiguous.

fields.name: Action / Record / Record ID
fields.meaning: Operation and affected record identity.
fields.values: Display labels plus recorded action code and record identifier where available.
fields.rules: Read-only; a dash means no value was recorded.

fields.name: Reason / Authority / Correlation ID
fields.meaning: Explanation, authorization context and identifier linking related diagnostics.
fields.values: Stored text or dash; correlation identifier.
fields.rules: Read-only; opening the panel shows full unclipped evidence.

fields.name: Changes (event panel)
fields.meaning: What the event changed: for each changed field, its value before and after, read from the record's own history when the event is opened. Audit events themselves never store values.
fields.values: Revision: the record's revision before → after. One line per changed field, as "old → new", with — for an empty or not yet recorded value. Patient, Birth date and Identifiers: the patient's current identification, for changes to a patient record. Recorded details: other facts stored with the event (codes, counts, IDs), labeled. Or one of these sentences: "No data changed." (an event with no record revision, such as a sign-in, a list or a check); "This revision changed no field value…" (the history was read and both revisions hold the same values, for example a laboratory profile saved with only a reason); "The values of this kind of record are not kept in a history…" (a revision was recorded but the record type keeps no readable history); "These are patient values, which your roles cannot read…" (field names are listed, each value shows Hidden).
fields.rules: Read-only. Old and new values are shown for patients (demographic corrections, identifiers added or deactivated, billing profile versions with address, phone, coverage and guarantor), the laboratory profile, clients, locations, practitioners and analytes, and for an instrument's Enabled and Transport. Patient values need View audit plus Enter orders or Manage quality (demographics and identifiers) or Enter orders or Billing (billing profile); without them only the changed field names are shown. Every opening is recorded as an access event; when patient values are shown it names the patient. Other record types show their revision only; result and report revisions, other configuration versions and instrument connection settings are not yet compared here.

fields.name: Chain intact / The chain is not intact
fields.meaning: Outcome of recomputing the selected stream’s chain.
fields.values: Count checked and findings such as hash mismatch, broken link, missing events, unknown algorithm or seal mismatch.
fields.rules: Read-only result for the checked stream, not merely the filtered rows.

actions.name: Open event / Previous / Next / Close
actions.does: Inspect the full details of already-loaded events, and what each changed.
actions.result: Read-only panel; events cannot be edited or deleted here. Opening an event reads its Changes from the record's history and records that read as an access event.

actions.name: Verify chain
actions.does: Recompute the chosen stream’s local integrity evidence.
actions.availableWhen: View audit authority and one stream chosen; with All streams the button is unavailable, because each stream has its own chain.
actions.result: Shows checked count and findings; it does not repair or rewrite events.

actions.name: Export › CSV, for analysis / PDF, for printing
actions.does: Saves every event that matches the current Stream and filters, not only the rows loaded on screen, to a new file in your Downloads folder: a CSV file for analysis or a PDF for printing or sending to an auditor. Each event lists stream, sequence number, occurred and recorded times (laboratory time zone; the CSV also in UTC), who acted, action, outcome, record, the patient for patient records, reason, authority, revision, its Changes as old → new values, the other recorded details and the correlation ID. The PDF also shows the laboratory, the filters used, the export time, who exported and the number of events, and says on every page when it contains patient information.
actions.availableWhen: Shown to users holding both View audit and Export (in the standard roles: Auditor together with Administrator). Patient values and identification are included only for patients the exporter's roles may read, as in the event panel; otherwise the changed field names are listed as hidden.
actions.result: A success notice names the file and the number of events. The file covers events recorded up to the moment of export; a CSV holds up to 50,000 events and a PDF up to 2,000. If more match, nothing is written and the page says to narrow the filters. The export is recorded in the Security stream (action Export events) with the format, number of events and patients, and every filter, so the same filters reproduce it; the file is never overwritten, a second export the same day gets a numbered name.

actions.name: Load older events
actions.does: Fetch the next older page matching the selected filters.
actions.result: Appends up to 100 events that come after the last row shown; events recorded since the first page do not shift it. A failed older-page load preserves rows already read.

actions.name: Clear filters / Show all events
actions.does: Remove every filter at once (record ID, action, By, Outcome, self-approvals, record type and days) except Stream.
actions.availableWhen: A filter is applied or no matching events are found.
actions.result: Reloads events for the selected stream, or for every stream.

actions.name: Audit anchors
actions.result: Navigates to anchor status and comparison.

restrictions: A local chain check cannot detect every rewritten chain or events removed from its end; compare separately held anchors.
Audit consistency does not establish that each recorded action was appropriate.
Do not remove or rewrite evidence to obtain a passing check.
An exported file leaves the application's protections: keep, send and dispose of it under the laboratory's procedure for records, especially when it contains patient information.
workflow: Start from All streams, or choose a stream, and narrow the review by record ID, action, who acted, outcome, record type and the days recorded.
Open relevant events and retain their sequence, actor, time and correlation identifiers.
Verify chain, then use Audit anchors when independent retained evidence is needed.
Investigate findings through the laboratory’s documented review process.

troubleshooting.recovery: Clear filters, choose All streams in case the event is in another stream, and verify the internal record identifier; load older events where available.

troubleshooting.problem: Older events could not be loaded
troubleshooting.recovery: Retry Load older events; current rows remain visible.
Preserve the result and event/sequence details and escalate through the laboratory’s incident process; do not alter evidence.

troubleshooting.problem: Changes says the values are hidden
troubleshooting.recovery: The event changed a patient record and your roles cannot read patients. Ask the laboratory's user administrator for a role with Enter orders or Manage quality (or Billing, for billing profile changes) if your review needs the values; the field names stay visible.

troubleshooting.problem: The changes could not be loaded
troubleshooting.recovery: Use Retry in the Changes section. The rest of the event stays visible; an event that no longer exists in the chosen stream shows "This audit event does not exist."

troubleshooting.problem: Not exported: more events match than one file holds
troubleshooting.recovery: Narrow the filters, for example choose one stream, fewer days (Recorded from / Recorded to), one user or one action, and export again; or use CSV, which holds more events than PDF.

troubleshooting.problem: Not exported: the Downloads folder is not available
troubleshooting.recovery: The computer's account has no Downloads folder the app can use. Ask the person who manages the computer to restore it, then export again.
Export needs the Export permission besides View audit. Ask the laboratory's user administrator for a role that holds it, if laboratory policy allows you to take audit records out of the application.

pages.title: Audit anchors
pages.purpose: Compare the local audit trail with retained seal fingerprints and inspect anchor export history.
pages.access: View audit authority reads and verifies anchors; Export anchors now additionally requires Backup and restore authority.

fields.name: Verify anchors / Anchor files tabs
fields.meaning: Switch between comparison results and export history.
fields.values: Verify anchors (default); Anchor files.
fields.rules: Tabs do not modify evidence.

fields.name: Anchor lag / Off-host targets / Last export
fields.meaning: Current delay in off-computer evidence, destination count and latest export.
fields.values: Minutes or Not reported; target count; timestamp/target or None yet.
fields.rules: Read-only. No off-host target means evidence is held only on this computer’s disks.

fields.name: Stream / Newest event / Sealed through event / Anchored through event
fields.meaning: Compare each stream’s latest event with its sealed and copied evidence boundaries.
fields.values: Security, Clinical and Access stream sequence numbers.
fields.rules: Read-only. Sealed locally is not the same as anchored off this computer.

fields.name: Oldest event not anchored off this computer
fields.meaning: Beginning of the unanchored interval.
fields.values: Timestamp or None.
fields.rules: Read-only; investigate prolonged lag.

fields.name: Anchors read / Anchors compared / Matching / Not matching
fields.meaning: Counts read and compared against the audit trail.
fields.values: Nonnegative counts.
fields.rules: Read-only; zero compared is not proof of a successful independent comparison.

fields.name: Covering events missing here / Conflicting anchors / Missing between others
fields.meaning: Potential missing local records, conflicting evidence or gaps in anchor sequence.
fields.values: Nonnegative counts with findings by stream and seal.
fields.rules: Read-only; these require investigation, not automatic dismissal.

fields.name: Explained by a restore / Explained by a restore not yet anchored / Seals not yet anchored
fields.meaning: Restore-related differences and evidence not yet exported.
fields.values: Nonnegative counts.
fields.rules: Read-only. Restore explanation does not itself account for the lost clinical work.

fields.name: Security / Clinical / Access chain
fields.meaning: Local-chain status checked during anchor verification.
fields.values: Intact; Not intact.
fields.rules: Read-only and distinct from anchor matching.

fields.name: Findings
fields.meaning: Meaning and location of each verification difference.
fields.values: Needs investigation or For information, with stream/seal range when known.
fields.rules: Includes mismatches, missing events, gaps, conflicts, lost interval, unanchored seals, foreign-installation evidence, invalid lines and unreadable files.

fields.name: Target / File name / Exported / Seals (Anchor files)
fields.meaning: Retained export destination, filename, time and seal ranges per stream.
fields.values: Recorded export facts; newest 100 files with an indication if older history exists.
fields.rules: Read-only; files are not modified after export.

actions.name: Export anchors now
actions.does: Write pending seal evidence to available targets.
actions.availableWhen: Backup and restore authority and configured targets.
actions.result: Reports seals/targets written and any failed or unavailable targets; missed anchors remain pending.

actions.name: Verify anchors
actions.does: Compare anchors on available targets with the local audit trail.
actions.availableWhen: View audit authority and reachable target evidence.
actions.result: Displays comparison counts, chain states and findings; verification is audited.

actions.name: Verify with anchors from another folder
actions.does: Use independently retained evidence from a chosen native folder.
actions.availableWhen: View audit authority; readable folder selected.
actions.result: Runs comparison; canceling folder selection verifies nothing.

restrictions: Anchor lag raises operational findings but does not itself block report release.
Anchors held on the same host provide limited protection against privileged changes on that host.
Anchors from another installation are reported and excluded from comparison; unreadable or invalid evidence is not silently a match.
workflow: Review lag and off-host target count.
Export pending anchors after confirming destination availability.
Verify against retained targets or another evidence folder and inspect both counts and findings.
Correlate restore-related differences with recovery records and investigate all unexplained differences.

troubleshooting.problem: No targets are available or a folder is unreadable
troubleshooting.recovery: Connect the expected media/share or choose the correct readable folder, then retry; preserve original evidence.
Read the failed/unavailable target counts, resolve access and retry export; pending anchors remain outstanding.

troubleshooting.problem: Anchors mismatch or local events are missing
troubleshooting.recovery: Preserve the retained files and comparison result, identify the stream/seal interval and involve the responsible investigator.
